title: Revised Preparation of a Mimetic Tissue Model for Quantitative Imaging Mass Spectrometry
protocol: Create a calibration curve with at least seven points including a blank.
Ensure the remaining six points cover the intended concentration range evenly.
Include a blank to assess detection capability, limit of blank (LoB), and limit of detection (LoD).
Prepare spiked homogenate samples for six levels.
Prepare one non-spiked homogenate sample.
Determine the minimum amount of homogenate needed.
Plan to have about 300-400 mg of homogenate for each layer.
Calculate that seven layers require a minimum of 2 g of tissue per model.
Prepare the tissue for homogenization.
Choose an appropriate sized tube/vial for large-scale homogenization of whole rat liver.
Portion enough tissue to satisfy the minimum amount required and fit into the chosen tube.
Do not overfill the tube; fill it about ¾ full to leave room for beads and homogenization.
Add stainless steel homogenizing beads to the tube (MP Metal Bead Lysing Matrix).
Roughly add 15 beads for a ¾ full 50 mL tube.
Wrap the top of the tube with parafilm to prevent tissue loss.
Homogenize the tissue using an MP FastPrep 24 or similar bead homogenizer.
Homogenize at 4 m/s for 30 seconds, repeating as necessary (usually 2-3 rounds).
Let the homogenate settle or spin down at low speed (1000 x g for ~ 30 s) to collect material from the tube walls.
Gently stir the mixture if using it directly after spinning down.
Combine homogenates from multiple tubes if tissue was spread over several tubes to avoid potential bias in sampling.
Aliquot the homogenate into smaller single use containers (~2 g each) to avoid multiple freeze/thaw cycles.
Trim the syringe barrel.
Pull back or remove the plunger.
Cut the luered tip off the syringe (can use an HPLC tubing cutter).
Trim the plunger seal.
Cut the conical tip off the plunger.
Re-insert the plunger into the syringe body to roughly the first volume demarcation.
Cut the extruding end of the plunger such that the bottom of the plunger is flush with the bottom of the syringe.
Drill or press a small hole through the bottom of the syringe barrel and plunger.
Press a small diameter L-shaped hexagonal (allen) key through the hole.
Maintain minimal solvent addition when spiking homogenates to preserve tissue morphology.
Keep the total volume of spiked standard below 2-3% (v/v) compared to the homogenate volume.
Ensure the solvent used to dissolve the standard is water miscible for efficient mixing with homogenized tissue.
Add consistent volumes of standard to each homogenate mimetic model layer.
Use a macro-enabled spreadsheet to determine appropriate volumes and concentrations of standards based on tissue homogenate weight and target concentration.
Add multiple standards to the same mimetic model if quantifying multiple species is necessary.
Invert concentration gradients when spiking multiple standards, with the highest concentration of one standard added at the lowest concentration level of another.
Keep total spiked volume below 2-3% (v/v) cutoff if possible.
Assess ion suppression resulting from the spiked standards for impact on other standards.
Do not use a stable isotopically labeled \(SIL) standard unless quantification is required for an endogenous species present in the tissue homogenate.
Use of SIL allows deconvolution of spiked standard levels from endogenous levels in the tissue homogenate.
Determine and assign the intended range and intervals for the final tissue concentration of each level of the mimetic model.
Record the weights of seven ~2 mL screw cap vials, one for each layer of the mimetic model.
Aliquot approximately 300 mg (~300 µL) of tissue homogenate into each pre-weighed vial using a positive displacement pipette.
Determine and prepare an appropriate dilution of stock standard to spike into each homogenate.
Ensure that the standard solution volume / tissue homogenate volume is ≤ 2-3% (v/v).
Dissolve the standard in a water miscible solvent to ensure mixing with homogenate.
Add the appropriate volume of standard to each homogenate and mix.
Add 1-2 metal homogenization beads to each vial once the standard has been added.
Mix at 4 m/s for ~30 seconds using FastPrep 24.
Spin down each spiked homogenate vial at 1000 x g for 30 seconds.
Prepare the freezing medium.
Set up a small beaker with dry ice-cooled ethanol deep enough to nearly submerge the mold.
Using a positive displacement pipette, collect about 250 μl of homogenate.
Wipe any excess homogenate off the pipette tip to avoid contaminating the edges of the mold.
Insert the pipette tip into the mold and expel enough of the homogenate to coat the plunger (or previous layer).
Tap the barrel flange side of the mold down onto a hard surface to remove air bubbles and/or help the homogenate to settle to an even layer.
Dip the mold into the dry ice-chilled ethanol for at least 1 minute until the newly added layer is frozen.
Repeat steps 2 and 3 for additional spiked homogenate layers.
Start with the blank layer, followed by the lowest concentration spiked homogenate, ending with the highest concentration.
Limit the time between freezing sequential layers to avoid contamination.
Add a fresh homogenate layer and freeze it as quickly as possible after addition to prevent mixing with previous layers.
Once the last layer is added and frozen, remove the handle (allen key).
Wrap the mold in foil.
Place the wrapped mold in a -80°C freezer for at least 3 hours or overnight.
Equilibrate the mimetic tissue model to the cryostat temperature as you would any other tissue.
Remove the model from the mold.
Use the palm of your hand to slightly warm the edges of the mold.
Slowly push the model out of the mold using any tool, such as forceps or a cut plunger.
Use the plunger to orient the tissue model for mounting to the chuck.
Carefully separate the plunger from the tissue model.
Apply a strip of mounting medium to the cryostat chuck.
Mount the mimetic model horizontally onto the chuck.
Section the model horizontally to avoid contamination between layers.
Trim into the mimetic model tissue until there is enough surface area to collect a section.
Section the model at the same thickness as the tissue to be quantified.
Thaw-mount onto the slide with the tissue to be quantified.
Replace remainder of the mimetic model back into the -80°C freezer for storage.
